claims.text: W-Ta-Cr-V is a high-entropy alloy system.
W-Ta-Cr-V is a refractory high-entropy alloy suitable for studying lattice heat conductivity.
The baseline W-Ta-Cr-V alloy can exist as a homogeneous, single-phase solid solution with minimal SRO or precipitate formation.
SRO precipitates scatter phonons more effectively than a fully homogeneous solid solution.
Controlled alloying, thermal treatment, or irradiation can promote SRO precipitate formation in the HEA.
SRO precipitates act as phonon-scattering centers.
SRO precipitates create local vibrational inhomogeneities.
Local vibrational inhomogeneities increase the phonon-scattering rate.
Increased phonon scattering reduces phonon lifetimes and mean free paths.
Reduced phonon lifetimes and mean free paths lower lattice thermal conductivity.
A greater density of SRO precipitates will produce measurably lower lattice thermal conductivity than the homogeneous baseline alloy.
Phonon conduction is less impeded in the homogeneous alloy with minimal SRO or precipitate formation.
The proposed effect is relevant under high-temperature or irradiation conditions where phonons contribute significantly to heat transport.
The effect is most relevant when lattice heat conduction dominates and the electronic contribution is relatively low.
Precipitate coarsening or substantial phase separation may alter the proposed conductivity effect.
The magnitude of the conductivity reduction depends on precipitate size, density, and spatial distribution.
The magnitude of the conductivity reduction depends on operating temperature and irradiation dose.
Laser-flash analysis or related techniques can be used to determine the lattice thermal conductivity for the proposed comparison.
TEM and/or XRD can quantify the size and density of the proposed SRO precipitates.
